method: Independent per-reading linguistic review against selected source senses, retained English cache object verification and fresh exact selected Spanish raw-line replay. Original model review; no native-human certification or fresh English archive replay.

approved.displayContext: A command to one person asking them to help the speaker.
approved.proofContext: Selected direct personal object me, not reflexive or dative composition. Exact source explicitly identifies ayudar combined with me; no generic me/te suffix rule.
approved.notes: Selected positive tú command with nonreflexive first-person object; no other personal-clitic rule.

approved.displayContext: An infinitive meaning to see one familiar addressee; the person doing the seeing is not specified.
approved.proofContext: Selected literal transitive sight sense with nonreflexive te→you. Does not license see yourself, reciprocal meanings, actor identity, SE rules or generic personal clitics.
approved.notes: Selected literal nonreflexive sight infinitive; te identifies one familiar object addressee, not the subject.

approved.displayContext: An infinitive meaning to see us; the person doing the seeing is not specified.
approved.proofContext: Selected literal transitive sight sense with nonreflexive nos→us. Does not license see ourselves/each other or infer a subject from the object.
approved.notes: Selected literal nonreflexive sight infinitive; nos identifies plural object, not subject or reciprocal action.

approved.displayContext: Clothes or clothing. English clothing stays uncountable, even though the Spanish form is plural.
approved.proofContext: Selected clothing collective sense. No pluralization of clothes into clotheses or clothing into clothings; does not globally override other meanings or English plural rules.
approved.notes: Collective clothing sense supports clothes/clothing without another plural suffix.

approved.displayContext: An abbreviation for pages, as in a reference to several pages of a book.
approved.proofContext: Exact source chain págs→pág→página, with explicit plural/abbreviation metadata. No punctuation removal, accent folding, inferred alias or expansion to other abbreviations.
approved.notes: Exact accented abbreviation chain supports pages; no punctuation or accent normalization.

approved.displayContext: Past existence: there was one thing, or there were several things. Spanish uses the singular form in this construction.
approved.proofContext: Selected impersonal existence only. English was/were follows the number of what existed; Spanish remains third singular. Not personal possession, perfect auxiliary, obligation or plural Spanish existential authority.
approved.notes: Impersonal existential third singular; English was/were are alternatives agreeing with the entity count.

approved.displayContext: Future existence: there will be something or some things. Spanish uses the singular form in this construction.
approved.proofContext: Selected future existence, not the conjectural perfect use habrá+participle. No actor possession or global HAVE rendering.
approved.notes: Selected future existence only; no perfect auxiliary or conjectural rendering.

approved.displayContext: Conditional existence: there would be something or some things under a condition.
approved.proofContext: Selects only third singular from the source first/third-person homograph. Impersonal existence, not I would have, possession, perfect auxiliary or conjectural perfect.
approved.notes: Selected third-singular conditional existence only, despite first-person homograph.

approved.displayContext: A selected hypothetical meaning: if there were something or some things. This is not a statement that they existed.
approved.proofContext: Selected simple hypothetical if-clause, not a universal translation of imperfect subjunctive. No omitted participle is invented: hubiera+participle perfect constructions remain separate and unsupported here. Select third singular only.
approved.notes: Selected hypothetical if-clause; not a past existence assertion or perfect construction.

approved.displayContext: A selected hypothetical meaning: if there were something or some things. This is not a statement that they existed.
approved.proofContext: Selected simple hypothetical if-clause, not a universal translation of imperfect subjunctive. No omitted participle is invented: hubiese+participle perfect constructions remain separate and unsupported here. Select third singular only.
approved.notes: Selected hypothetical if-clause; not a past existence assertion or perfect construction.

approved.displayContext: Describes a past habit or regular occurrence. This phrase normally needs a following action, such as another verb.
approved.proofContext: English used to is the explicitly imperfect-only source sense of soler, not ordinary use and not a blanket imperfect translation. These are alternative word-level auxiliary fragments, not complete sentences. Selected literal first/third-person readings exclude formal-you substitution.
approved.notes: Explicit imperfect-only habitual source supports auxiliary fragments used to; no following action invented.

approved.displayContext: They regularly did something in the past. The English phrase normally needs a following action.
approved.proofContext: Selected literal they, not formal-you ustedes. Explicit imperfect-only source sense of soler, not ordinary use; word-level auxiliary fragment, no invented following action.
approved.notes: Explicit imperfect-only habitual source and literal third-plural they support incomplete auxiliary fragment.

guards: Admit only these exact whole-word/source/sense/grammar bindings if independently approved; no generic clitic, pronoun, alias, existential or auxiliary rule follows.
No suffix decomposition, accent folding, punctuation stripping, actor/object invention or arbitrary English lemma substitution.
AYÚDAME/VERTE/VERNOS are selected nonreflexive personal-object readings; all other SE/reflexive/dative/argument holds remain.
ROPAS has only selected lexical clothes/clothing English outputs; no automatic double pluralization or global mass-noun policy.
PÁGS uses only the exact source plural abbreviation chain to page; no inferred spelling aliases.
All five HABER readings select impersonal third singular existence. Never actor possession, first-person output, Spanish plural existence, perfect/obligation construction or a global HAVE permission.
HUBIERA/HUBIESE use explicitly labelled selected hypothetical if-clauses, not all-context equivalents or invented had-been constructions.
SOLER equivalents are incomplete grammatical auxiliary fragments requiring a following action. No blanket used to for arbitrary Spanish imperfects, and no ordinary-English USE inflection.
All existing role/SE/argument/auxiliary holds remain archived and in force; these materially specific proposals do not silently override them.
Source-casework/proofContext stay audit-only; only approved displayContext and selected grammatical values may be learner-facing.
No app/code/pool/answer/save/lesson changes, publication or runtime AI requests.
packagingGuidance: Package only the closed selected lexical proposal and review, with pinned evidence/attribution and source checker. Original broader Spanish inventory can remain local; no generic clitic, alias, auxiliary, existential or inflection authority.
